## Merged Code Contributions to Open-Source Projects

[My GitHub pull requests](https://github.com/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Ajooyoungseo+archived%3Afalse+is%3Aclosed) have been peer-reviewed and merged into active open-source data science projects:
\keepwithnext

* Quarto, Visual Studio Code extension (Posit PBC, 2023): added diagram executable cell engines (quarto-dev/quarto #92).

* quarto-webr, Quarto extension for WebR (2023): improved accessibility by replacing the CodeMirror editor with the Monaco code editor (coatless/quarto-webr #16).

* vscode-R, R extension for Visual Studio Code (2022): contributed R and R Markdown snippets (vscode-R #1009, #1012, #1084, and #1085).

* rticles, article formats for R Markdown (2021): added the reproducible Journal of Educational Data Mining article template (rticles #251; released in v0.21).

* shiny, web application framework for R (2020): contributed to improving keyboard and TTS accessibility for input widgets.

* vitae, curriculum vitae for R Markdown (2020): contributed to enabling LaTeX engine customization and to displaying multiple bibliographies based on a Lua filter.

* rmarkdown, dynamic documents for R (2019): contributed to improving ioslides_presentation accessibility for screen reading software.

* bookdown, authoring books and technical documents with R Markdown (2019): developed nine output-format functions (context_document2, github_document2, beamer_presentation2, and six others) that let R Markdown users cross-reference figures and tables.

* distill, R Markdown format for scientific and technical writing (2019): improved screen reader accessibility for the navigation bar; contributed to displaying more metadata for journal article entries; added missing Google Scholar meta tags.

* wordcountaddin, word counts and readability statistics in R Markdown documents (2019): contributed to the text_stats() function, which gives a word count and other statistics for selected text.

* BrailleR, improved access for blind users (2019): contributed to the BRLThis() function, which lets blind R users convert a graph into a PDF ready for embossing in braille.
